rules.title: Application screening fee cap (Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6)
rules.requirement: A landlord may charge an application screening fee only to cover actual out-of-pocket costs of gathering information on the applicant and the reasonable value of time spent, and never more than $30 per applicant (adjustable annually for CPI increases since January 1, 1998).

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to landlords (owners of residential rental property) and their agents charging applicants, including guarantors and cosigners, for residential rental units.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Does not preempt provisions governing collection of deposits and fees under federal or state housing assistance programs.

rules.interaction: Applies notwithstanding Section 1950.5; the fee is not 'security' under 1950.5. Does not preempt federal or state housing assistance program rules on deposits and fees.
rules.quoted_span: In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant.

rules.title: No screening fee when no unit available
rules.requirement: A landlord or agent may not charge an application screening fee when they know or should have known that no rental unit is available or will be available within a reasonable period of time.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to landlords and agents charging applicants for residential rental units.

rules.quoted_span: A landlord or their agent shall not charge an applicant an application screening fee when they know or should have known that no rental unit is available at that time or will be available within a reasonable period of time.

rules.title: Conditions for charging screening fee: first-come process or full refund
rules.requirement: A landlord may charge a screening fee only if, when collecting it, it offers either a first-come-first-served screening process under written criteria (approving the first qualified applicant and charging only applicants whose applications are actually considered), or a process returning the entire fee to any applicant not selected within 7 days of selecting a tenant or 30 days of application, whichever is first.
rules.key_value: Refund within 7 days of selection or 30 days of application, whichever first

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to landlords and agents charging screening fees to applicants for residential rental units.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Inadvertent collection from concurrent submissions requires refund within seven days; no refund required to applicants denied after consideration under the first-come process.

rules.quoted_span: (B) An application screening process in which the landlord or their agent returns the entire screening fee to any applicant who is not selected for tenancy, regardless of the reason, within 7 days of selecting an applicant for tenancy or 30 days of when the application was submitted, whichever occurs first.

rules.title: Screening fee receipt and return of unused fee
rules.requirement: The landlord must give the applicant an itemized receipt of out-of-pocket expenses and time spent, must return any portion of the fee not used for authorized purposes if no reference check or credit report is obtained, and must provide a copy of the credit report to the applicant within seven days of receiving it.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to landlords and agents who collect application screening fees for residential rentals.

rules.quoted_span: The landlord or their agent shall provide, personally, or by mail, the applicant with a receipt for the fee paid by the applicant, which receipt shall itemize the out-of-pocket expenses and time spent by the landlord or their agent to obtain and process the information about the applicant.
